definition: An assessment of climate and disaster risk to the project's digital assets, done for this project or required of others: site-specific assessments of works, sector or national assessments of telecom infrastructure, assessments operators must conduct, or hazard mapping used to plan the network.
note: Trial set: six measures used to test the candidates stage against hand-graded sentences.

measure_name: Underground or aerial fibre for hazard resilience
definition: Choosing how fibre or cable is laid because of hazards: buried or in ducts and conduits to protect it from storms and floods, aerial where floods or landslides make burial worse, or the choice made route by route according to risk.
note: Trial set: six measures used to test the candidates stage against hand-graded sentences.

measure_name: ID or registries linked to shock response
definition: A stated link between an ID system, civil registry or social registry and a shock or disaster response: integration or data exchange with beneficiary or disaster registries, ID used to target emergency payments, backups of ID records, or registration after disasters. An outcome alone ('the ID will enable faster relief') is not the measure.
note: Trial set: six measures used to test the candidates stage against hand-graded sentences.

definition: Early warning of hazards: alerts sent to people (SMS, cell broadcast, apps, portals), the monitoring and forecasting that feeds them, warning equipment such as sirens, or an early warning strategy.

definition: Redundancy so service survives the loss of one part: diverse or alternative cable routes and ring topology, a second submarine cable, a disaster recovery site or second data centre, cloud hosting spread across regions, or failover.
